title: Redwood discovery - reliability & fallbacks with Silverline Commerce
summary: Intro discovery to understand Silverline's reliability needs for customer-facing inference: multi-region failover, regional SLAs, private deployment constraints for PCI, and fallback model policies to balance cost and latency.

Run a 1-week latency/cost benchmark using Silverline sample traffic (Arjun to provision)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Arjun Rao (Redwood SE), Hannah Lee (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (CTO - Silverline), Marcus Delgado (Head of Infra), Priya Singh (SRE), Evan Cho (Product)

Summary: quick discovery on reliability, incident tolerance, fallbacks, and deployment mode considerations (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

00:00 Lena Torres: okay thanks everyone for joining, we just wanted to understand how Redwood handles outages and incident tolerance especially since we are trading off latency and cost across our checkout flows
00:12 Maya Patel: yeah great, thanks Lena, quick intro, I'm Maya AE, Arjun and Hannah are our SEs, we'll walk through typical patterns and hear your constraints, then talk about fallbacks and multi-region routing
00:25 Marcus Delgado: our biggest worry is a provider-side incident during peak seasonal traffic — we need graceful degradation not full failures, and we have PCI requirements so private network options matter
00:40 Arjun Rao: totally, so two axes we typically look at: routing/failover and model-level fallbacks. For routing you can do multi-region active-passive or active-active with health checks; we also support automated regional failover policies
00:58 Priya Singh: can you clarify automated failover? like does Redwood reroute to another region automatically or do we need a load balancer in front?
01:10 Hannah Lee: Redwood can handle smart routing at the control plane — you set policies (latency-first, cost-first, strict-region). For Hosted customers default is region-aware routing, and for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own LB or use our routing with SSO/VPC peering. There's also an option to failover to a cheaper model family if the preferred cluster is saturated
01:34 Evan Cho: cheaper model family meaning lower-cost quantized variant? what's the quality delta on that?
01:42 Arjun Rao: yes often a quantized or smaller model; we recommend a graded fallback chain — e.g., gpt-like-16k -> gpt-like-8k-quant -> retrieval + small model. We measure quality regressions with a prompt set so you know expected deltas
02:00 Lena Torres: that sounds useful, but we need strict SLAs for checkout - 99.95%? We have internal target of 99.99% during business hours for the critical flow
02:15 Maya Patel: we offer SLAs on Dedicated customers — typical uptime SLA is 99.9 to 99.99 depending on contract and geography. Hosted tiers have commercial SLAs for enterprise plans; Private deployments we can negotiate a platform SLA but usually the infra owner is on you so we focus on support SLAs and runbooks
02:36 Marcus Delgado: for private we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs retained 12 months, any blockers?
02:44 Hannah Lee: we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM via partner), and audit logs with configurable retention. For Private deployments we can include a customer-managed control plane in a VPC or an on-prem package. We have a checklist we'll share
02:58 Priya Singh: in an incident if the primary region loses connectivity, can the KV cache be warm in the failover region? is prefix caching replicated?
03:10 Arjun Rao: good question—prefix/KV cache replication depends on deployment. Hosted: we have cross-region cache priming options, but it's eventual; Dedicated/Private: you can configure synchronous replication across racks or regions but there's a cost/latency tradeoff. Often customers allow a short cold-start while we rehydrate cache from durable storage, and we use batching to reduce tail impacts
03:34 Lena Torres: what's the expected cold-start latency if cache misses during failover? like ms vs seconds?
03:42 Arjun Rao: typically a small model warmup is tens to a couple hundred ms, but if KV cache is empty and the model needs to regen big kv states it can be multiple seconds. That's why we recommend a fallback that serves slightly lower-fidelity responses but within latency SLOs for checkout paths
04:05 Marcus Delgado: any example policies you recommend for ecom checkout?
04:12 Hannah Lee: for checkout flows we see customers use 'latency-first' with model fallback after 200ms tail, and region failover only after 2x health-check misses or sustained error rate. Also keep read-only caches in a global store (redis geo-replication) to speed recovery
04:30 Lena Torres: on deployment mode — what are the pros and cons for us? we are considering Hosted to move fast, Dedicated if we need guaranteed throughput, Private for PCI compliance
04:43 Maya Patel: Hosted is fastest for time to value, we handle most infra and provide observability. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and an SLA for throughput/latency—best if you have predictable traffic and compliance needs. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full network control and satisfies strict PCI/regulatory requirements; Redwood still provides the control plane optionally and we integrate with your KMS and audit tools
05:05 Priya Singh: do you support canary deploys and automatic rollback if a model regresses?
05:12 Arjun Rao: yes, rollouts are first-class: canaries, A/B, gradual traffic shifts, automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to prompt sets and eval metrics; we also have tracing hooks to tie errors to specific model versions
05:30 Evan Cho: we'd want deterministic routing for some customers in EU for data residency — can policies be per-customer-route?
05:38 Hannah Lee: absolutely, per-route policies with tenant tags; you can force EU-only processing and have different fallback chains per route, e.g., EU-only fallback to smaller EU-hosted model before failing to non-EU region
05:55 Marcus Delgado: what about cost controls during failover? if all regions failover to Dedicated expensive clusters, costs could spike
06:03 Maya Patel: good point — you can set budget caps and fallback rules: e.g., failover to cheaper model or reduce max tokens in the response, or route a subset of traffic to degraded mode. Redwood Optimize provides suggestions to avoid runaway costs
06:18 Priya Singh: auditability in incidents — do you provide a post-mortem package? logs, traces, and token-level cost/latency breakdowns?
06:30 Arjun Rao: yes we provide per-request traces, token-level breakdown, per-route dashboards and an incident export package for enterprise accounts. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your SIEM and ship audit logs per retention policy
06:45 Lena Torres: got it. one operational question: during a provider upgrade or patch window, do you give maintenance windows or can we opt for pinned versions?
06:55 Hannah Lee: you can pin model versions and control rollout windows. For Dedicated we coordinate maintenance windows; for Private you fully control upgrades unless you opt into managed updates
07:08 Marcus Delgado: we'd like to run a benchmark with our checkout traffic pattern; if Redwood can run it in Hosted and in a Dedicated preview, that would help procurement decisioning
07:19 Maya Patel: absolutely we can do a two-arm benchmark: Hosted baseline and Dedicated cluster with your provisioning. Arjun will own setting up the harness and Hannah will put together routing policy recommendations
07:30 Priya Singh: small note, we need to ensure test harness masks PII and card data; we'll send a sanitized sample stream
07:38 Maya Patel: perfect — please share sanitized samples, Arjun will give instructions for masking and ingestion format
07:44 Lena Torres: any risks we should be aware of when using multi-region active-active?
07:51 Arjun Rao: data consistency and KV cache staleness are main ones; also cross-region tail latency and cost. Active-active gives lower latency but increases complexity — we usually recommend sticky routing with quick failover for checkout to keep consistency
08:09 Evan Cho: timeline wise we want a pilot by end of June and procurement by mid-July, is that feasible?
08:16 Maya Patel: yes that's reasonable. quick recap and next steps after Qs
08:22 Lena Torres: one more question on legal: do you support standard DPA + SSO (SAML/SCIM)?
08:28 Hannah Lee: yes, SAML, SCIM, RBAC, enterprise DPA templates, plus custom clauses for Dedicated/Private if needed
08:36 Maya Patel: recap: we'll send security pack and private deployment checklist, Arjun will set up benchmark, Hannah will send recommended routing policies + topology diagram, and we'll schedule Dedicated pricing review with finance. Expect docs by 2026-06-11 and benchmark ready by 2026-06-16
08:52 Lena Torres: perfect, thanks everyone
08:54 Marcus Delgado: thanks
08:55 Meeting end.
